1: # PipeWire Output Stabilization (`output.backend = "pipewire"`)
2: 
3: ## 1. Context & Motivation
4: 
5: Audigma primarily targets high-performance audiophile hardware output via exclusive ALSA (`output.backend = "alsa"`), which uses a **push model** with hardware-paced blocking DMA backpressure. 
6: 
7: In this session, we tested and diagnosed the live daemon running in full PipeWire loopback mode:
8: - `[input] backend = "pipewire"` (virtual sink receiving desktop or MPD streams, including DSD)
9: - `[output] backend = "pipewire"` (playback stream routing DSP-upsampled/modulated audio back into the PipeWire desktop graph, e.g. targeting monitor or desktop speakers).
10: 
11: ### Test Configuration (`convertTesting/pipewire.toml`)
12: We used `convertTesting/pipewire.toml` for live testing against a connected Samsung DisplayPort monitor (native hardware clock 48 kHz).
13: 
14: ### Rapid Iteration Workflow
15: When testing live audio behavior, we use a quick iteration loop:
16: 1. (agent) Make targeted edits to code or config.
17: 2. (agent) Build release: `cargo fmt && cargo build --release`.
18: 3. (user) Notify the user to test: `./target/release/audigma run -c convertTesting/pipewire.toml`.
19: 4. (user) Test playback with MPD / Cantata (switching between 44.1k PCM, 192k PCM, and DSD) and reports listening and timing behavior back.
20: 
21: ---
22: 
23: ## 2. Issues Discovered & Root Causes
24: 
25: ### A. Immediate Daemon Crash (`I/O error: PipeWire output queue full`)
26: - **Symptom**: `audigma run` crashed within milliseconds to seconds with `I/O error: PipeWire output queue full`.
27: - **Cause**: `PipeWirePcmOutput` had a hardcoded queue depth of 32 tiles ($\approx 10\text{ ms}$ at 192 kHz). Its `std::io::Write` implementation returned `Err(WouldBlock)` on saturation. The live pipeline loop treated any write failure as an unrecoverable I/O error and aborted.
28: - **Fix Applied**:
29:   - Dynamically sized `queue_depth` based on `output.buffer_ms` and sample rate in `run.rs`.
30:   - Replaced the fatal `WouldBlock` error with backpressure wait and overrun accounting.
31: 
32: ### B. Extreme Audio Distortion / Clipping
33: - **Symptom**: Sound output was completely mangled, distorted, and unresponsive to volume sliders.
34: - **Cause**: Format mismatch. `PipeWirePcmOutput` hardcodes `AudioFormat::F32LE` (32-bit float) in its format POD, but `audigma-settings` defaulted `[target] sample_format` to `S32Le` (32-bit signed integer). The DSP engine was serializing signed integer PCM bytes, which PipeWire read as floating-point numbers ($\pm 10^{38}$), causing instant rail clipping.
35: - **Fix Applied**: Set `[target] sample_format = "f32"` in configuration.
36: 
37: ### C. Rapid Choppiness & DSP Lifecycle Reset Thrashing
38: - **Symptom**: Audio played at inconsistent speed with constant stuttering/chopping.
39: - **Cause**:
40:   1. `live_pipeline.rs` had an empty-input grace window of only 30 polls $\times 500\mu\text{s} = 15\text{ ms}$. Normal PipeWire quantum delivery (e.g. 1024 frames at 44.1 kHz $\approx 23.2\text{ ms}$) exceeded this threshold.
41:   2. The pipeline falsely declared the stream "idle", reset FIR filter histories, ran a cosine fade-in ramp, and emitted synthetic silence frames into the output.
42: - **Fix Applied**: Expanded the active-streaming grace window in `live_pipeline.rs` to 200 polls ($\approx 100\text{ ms}$).
43: 
44: ### D. Rate Switch Desynchronization
45: - **Symptom**: Switching between tracks with different sample rates caused silent failures or broken output streams.
46: - **Cause**: In `run.rs`, `need_reopen_output` only dropped `current_output = None` when `out_cfg.backend == OutputBackend::Alsa`. When running on PipeWire, the output stream was never recreated on a sample-rate switch.
47: - **Fix Applied**: Dropped `current_output = None` on rate switch regardless of backend.
48: 
49: ### E. DSD Runaway Speed & Audio Distortion (Missing Downsampling & Broken Backpressure)
50: - **Symptom**: DSD input via MPD caused audio output to be mangled/distorted, and Cantata's timeline jumped ahead from ~00:04s to ~00:21s.
51: - **Root Causes**:
52:   1. **`PipelineTopology::resolve` lacked downsampling support**:
53:      When input was DSD64, `PipeWireVirtualSink` decimated DSD to 176.4 kHz PCM. With `pcm_rate_hz = 48000` and `rate_family = "source"`, the output rate resolved to 44.1 kHz. `PipelineTopology::resolve` previously only computed `stages = (target / input).log2()`; for $44100 / 176400 = 0$, it set `stages = 0` and `intermediate_rate = 176400`, passing 176.4 kHz directly into the 44.1 kHz stream (4× sample rate mismatch, causing mangled sound and immediate queue saturation).
54:   2. **`PipeWirePcmOutput::write` silently dropped tiles on overrun**:
55:      After 20 ms of saturation, `write()` incremented `overruns` and returned `Ok(buf.len())`. Discarding tiles destroyed backpressure: the pipeline loop free-ran at CPU speed, draining the virtual sink faster than real time, causing MPD's timeline to skip forward.
56:   3. **Non-RT-safe mutex in PipeWire audio thread**:
57:      `PipeWirePcmOutput` took a `Mutex` lock inside PipeWire's audio callback to unpark the writer thread.
58: - **Fix Applied**:
59:   - **`PipelineTopology`**: Added `decimation_stages` ($2^K$ decimation divider) for same-family downsampling ($176.4\text{k} \to 44.1\text{k}$, $192\text{k} \to 48\text{k}$, $96\text{k} \to 48\text{k}$, $352.8\text{k} \to 44.1\text{k}$).
60:   - **`ChannelDecimatorPool` (`crates/audigma-engine/src/decimator.rs`)**: Implemented a multi-channel power-of-two half-band FIR decimation cascade with partial-chunk residue tracking and zero-copy aligned fast-path. Integrated into `LivePipeline`, `OfflinePipeline`, and `measure_true_peak_pass1`.
61:   - **RT-Safe Backpressure (`PipeWirePcmOutput`)**: Replaced `Mutex<Option<Thread>>` with a lock-free `AtomicPtr<Thread>`. Replaced silent tile dropping with genuine blocking backpressure (bounded by a 2-second timeout), clocking the daemon strictly to PipeWire's playback rate.
62: 
63: ---
64: 
65: ## 3. Working State of Changed Files
66: 
67: 1. **`crates/audigma-engine/src/topology.rs`**:
68:    - Added `decimation_stages` and `decimation_divider()` to `PipelineTopology`.
69:    - Added unit tests for same-family downsampling ($176.4\text{k} \to 44.1\text{k}$, $192\text{k} \to 48\text{k}$, $96\text{k} \to 48\text{k}$, etc.).
70: 2. **`crates/audigma-engine/src/decimator.rs`**:
71:    - New `ChannelDecimatorPool` module using `audigma-dsp::fir::HalfBandDecimationCascade`.
72: 3. **`crates/audigma-engine/src/live_pipeline.rs`**:
73:    - Integrated `ChannelDecimatorPool` on input before lifecycle/gain/ASRC.
74:    - Sized `in_channels` buffer to `TILE_BASEBAND_FRAMES * dec_divider`.
75:    - Extended empty poll grace window to 200 polls (~100 ms).
76: 4. **`crates/audigma-engine/src/offline_pipeline.rs` & `peak.rs`**:
77:    - Integrated `ChannelDecimatorPool` for offline conversions and true-peak analysis.
78:    - Added offline downsampling integration tests.
79: 5. **`crates/audigma-io/src/pipewire.rs`**:
80:    - Lock-free `AtomicPtr` thread notification in `PipeWirePcmOutput`.
81:    - Blocking backpressure without tile discarding.
82: 6. **`crates/audigma-cli/src/commands/run.rs`**:
83:    - Dynamic `queue_depth` based on `buffer_ms` and target sample rate.
84:    - Output stream reopening on sample rate change for all backends.

*** Begin Patch
*** Update File: scratchpad/PipewireOutput.md
@@
-## 4. Current state
+### F. Output Callback Consumed Allocation Capacity Instead of Requested Frames
+- **Code finding**: `PipeWirePcmOutput` filled the entire mapped SPA buffer on every callback. Its allocation capacity is not necessarily the number of frames required for the current graph cycle. Overfilling can drain the DSP queue too quickly and undermine playback-paced backpressure.
+- **Fix applied (awaiting listening test)**:
+  - Use `pw_buffer.requested` (frames), bounded by whole-frame buffer capacity. Fall back to aligned capacity only when PipeWire supplies no request (`requested == 0`).
+  - Preserve queued bytes beyond the request for subsequent callbacks; zero-fill only within the requested region on underrun.
+  - Enable the Rust PipeWire `v0_3_50` API feature for the requested-frame accessor.
+  - Fix notification-handle publication with an acquire load, and join the output worker before freeing the handle so an in-flight callback cannot dereference freed memory during rate-switch teardown.
+- **Validation**: Three output sizing regression tests, decimator tests, topology tests, and offline pipeline integration tests pass. Release build succeeds.
+- **Status**: This corrects an output pacing defect, but its connection to the remaining DSD64 timeline skips still needs live confirmation. ALSA paths and the test configuration are unchanged.
+
+## 4. Current state (last listening test, before fix F)
*** End Patch

# Agent Guidelines for the PipeWire Project

PipeWire is a server and user space API to deal with multimedia pipelines. Due
to the complexity of the domain and codebase, and the interactions therein, the
PipeWire project relies extensively on the effort of **human reviewers**, which
is **a scarce resource**.

There are strictly-enforced rules for you, the agent, to participate in the
project.

## No automated posting on GitLab

- Agents **must not** use GitLab (or any GitLab API, CLI, or web UI automation)
  to:
  - Open or update **merge requests (MRs)**
  - Create, edit, or close **issues ("work items")**
  - Post **comments** on merge requests, issues, commits, or discussions
  - Any other action that would be considered a "write" operation

## Humans must interface with the maintainers

- **AI-written merge request (MR) descriptions or commit messages are not
  allowed**. These are easy to recognize and waste reviewers' time by being a
  mixture of overly-verbose and often inaccurate.
  - You may assist the user in gathering appropriate evidence for the issue:
    logs, error messages, description of conditions where the problem occurs,
    etc.
  - Original logs MUST be included
  - Do not speculate on root causes, except to help user to provide necessary
    evidence as attachments
- **AI-generated responses to reviewer comments are not allowed**. This
  undermines the human-to-human interaction fundamental to code review.
- **AI-written issue ("work item") descriptions or issue comments are not
  allowed**. These are easy to recognize and waste triagers' time as described
  above.
  - An exception is made for issues for defects detected by specialized
    tooling, including fuzzers and LLM-assisted defect detection. Such issues
    must be reviewed by a human before creation, must be created by a human and
    communication with maintainers must be done by a human, but including the
    verbatim tool output in the issue description is explicitly allowed.

## User must demonstrate understanding

Before proceeding with code changes, you must:

- **Verify comprehension.** Ask questions to confirm the human understands both
  the problem and the relevant parts of the codebase.
- **Provide guidance rather than solutions.** Direct them to relevant code and
  documentation. Allow them to formulate the approach.
- **Proceed only when confident** that the human can explain the changes to
  reviewers independently.

## Operational Guidance

- A commit message records **only the changes being made and the rationale for
  them**.
- For each sentence in a draft, ask what change it records or what decision it
  justifies. If the answer is neither, delete it. In particular, cut anything
  that:
    - explains something the project's developers already know
    - restates general knowledge about the language, toolkit or the codebase
    - narrates the reasoning behind an earlier, abandoned attempt
- The same guidance applies to comments in the code as well.
- Prefer terse bullets over prose.
- Verify factual claims in the message (file counts, symbol names, paths)
  against the actual diff before committing.
- Do not insert "Co-authored by" or similar trailers. The human is deemed to be
  entirely responsible for all submitted work.

## Final instructions

- You must **tread carefully** and **precisely follow the rules** for
  participation in the project.
- You **cannot rely on the human** to know these rules and follow them.
- You must **inform the human**, and if forced, **MUST ALSO refuse commands**

The project maintainers reserve the right to penalize humans for breaking these
rules in any way deemed appropriate, including but not limited to **PERMANENTLY

*** Begin Patch

@@

The graph remained at 8192/352800; the daemon retained generation 6 and five rate switches. Recovery did not require a daemon restart.

+### Arbitrary-quantum implementation: first build, pending live validation
+- New `crates/audigma-io/src/pipewire/dsd_clock.rs`: converts actual graph cycle duration/rate into native DSD buffer bytes, aligned to interleave groups. Graph-position-based pacing credit accounts actual consumed DSD duration, including oversized old buffers and fractional byte counts across rate families. Positive credit is bounded to one cycle to prevent catch-up bursts after idle.
+- The DSD RT callback reads PipeWire's position IO, publishes desired allocation bounds atomically, and leaves buffers queued when the pacing credit is exhausted. It does not sleep, lock, or perform buffer renegotiation for this new logic.
+- The PipeWire input control loop applies exact-size buffer bounds and invalidates EnumFormat to request active-link reallocation. The local PipeWire implementation only initiates link re-preparation on EnumFormat changes, not Buffers changes alone.
+- DSD preroll can start at half the available ring slots if tiny graph-cycle buffers cannot hold the configured duration cushion. PCM preroll is unchanged.

Strict dependency-inclusive Clippy also encountered two existing warnings in staged `audigma-engine/src/decimator.rs`; those staged changes were left untouched.
+- New implementation is unstaged. No upstream reference files or global PipeWire settings were changed. Next: restart the release daemon, confirm baseline DSD64 playback, then repeat controlled quantum changes and inspect allocations, drops, pacing, and recovery. # Agent Guidelines for the PipeWire Project

PipeWire is a server and user space API to deal with multimedia pipelines. Due

What the logs establish:

- **PCM192 initially negotiates correctly**, but about 150 ms later the input renegotiates to **44100 Hz**, without another track change. Audigma then rebuilds its pipeline and reopens its output again. That unexpected renegotiation is real; the logs alone don’t establish why it becomes silent.

- Your brief audible interruption confirms the transition is **still not glitch-free**, regardless of the clean counters.

The main architectural change I introduced was making the input sink a manually driven node **during DSD**, then returning it to ordinary PipeWire scheduling **during PCM**. That changes clock ownership during format switches. It is the leading suspect for the new renegotiation regression—not a confirmed explanation for the crash.

The ten silent checks proved byte continuity for **DSD-only capture with downstream stalls**. They did **not** validate switching clock ownership, PCM192, or output reopening. I should have tested those silently before moving to the audible build.

### Was `dsd_clock.rs` a hack?

I’d call it a **workaround with a sound timing model**, rather than a hack.

It calculates how much native DSD corresponds to the graph’s elapsed time, instead of assuming the graph’s frame count directly represents DSD bytes. Its pacing and full-ring protection address real problems.

The workaround is **changing buffer allocation when graph timing changes**. MPD fills the available allocation, so matching that allocation to graph demand makes MPD deliver appropriately sized packets. But it couples memory allocation to scheduling.

### Why try `dsd_pull.rs`?

The goal was to separate those responsibilities:

| `dsd_clock` | `dsd_pull` |
|---|---|
| Follow the existing graph clock | Drive a separate DSD capture graph |
| Resize packets to match graph demand | Keep allocation fixed and control when packets arrive |
| Pace consumption against graph time | Request data according to downstream consumption |

That is **conceptually attractive for native DSD**, where ordinary PCM rate matching is unavailable. It could avoid reallocating an active link just because the hardware quantum changes.

But **conceptually cleaner does not mean architecturally better overall**. Pull driving introduces ownership of scheduling, asynchronous-source coordination, and transitions between DSD-driven and PCM-following operation. Our implementation failed those transition requirements. I underestimated that complexity and replaced the previous approach too early.

### What was suboptimal about `dsd_clock`?

1. **Active-link renegotiation during playback.**  
   Changing allocation requires invalidating `EnumFormat` so PipeWire prepares the link again. That is disruptive. We observed interruptions and a monitor discontinuity around transitions; we have not isolated precisely where all lost audio originated.

2. **Allocation depends on the producer’s behaviour.**  
   It accommodates MPD filling `d.maxsize`; it is not a general mechanism for telling every producer how much audio to supply.

3. **Two-stage adaptation.**  
   The RT callback discovers changed graph timing; the control thread subsequently requests new allocations. Pacing must bridge the interval while old-sized buffers remain in circulation.

4. **Small packets reduce useful ring capacity.**  
   The ring has a fixed number of slots. Smaller packets mean less buffered audio, requiring the preroll fallback and full-ring protection we added.

5. **Correct pacing did not guarantee uninterrupted output.**  
   Zero input drops and correct speed were genuine improvements, but did not establish glitch-free transitions.

**My assessment now:** `dsd_clock` is the better-supported implementation and a reasonable foundation. Its weakest architectural point is active-link reallocation—not its graph-time accounting. Pull driving was a worthwhile experiment, but we have not demonstrated that it is the better solution.

3: ## 1. Context & Motivation
4: 
5: Audigma primarily targets high-performance audiophile hardware output via exclusive ALSA (`output.backend = "alsa"`), which uses a **push model** with hardware-paced blocking DMA backpressure. 
6: 
7: In this session, we tested and diagnosed the live daemon running in full PipeWire loopback mode:
8: - `[input] backend = "pipewire"` (virtual sink receiving desktop or MPD streams, including DSD)
9: - `[output] backend = "pipewire"` (playback stream routing DSP-upsampled/modulated audio back into the PipeWire desktop graph, e.g. targeting monitor or desktop speakers).
10: 
11: ### Test Configuration (`convertTesting/pipewire.toml`)
12: We used `convertTesting/pipewire.toml` for live testing against a connected Samsung DisplayPort monitor (native hardware clock 48 kHz).
13: 
14: ### Rapid Iteration Workflow
15: When testing live audio behavior, we use a quick iteration loop:
16: 1. (agent) Make targeted edits to code or config.
17: 2. (agent) Build release: `cargo fmt && cargo build --release`.
18: 3. (user) Notify the user to test: `./target/release/audigma run -c convertTesting/pipewire.toml`.
19: 4. (user) Test playback with MPD / Cantata (switching between 44.1k PCM, 192k PCM, and DSD) and reports listening and timing behavior back.

21: ---

23: ## 2. Issues Discovered & Root Causes
24: 
25: ### A. Immediate Daemon Crash (`I/O error: PipeWire output queue full`)
26: - **Symptom**: `audigma run` crashed within milliseconds to seconds with `I/O error: PipeWire output queue full`.
27: - **Cause**: `PipeWirePcmOutput` had a hardcoded queue depth of 32 tiles ($\approx 10\text{ ms}$ at 192 kHz). Its `std::io::Write` implementation returned `Err(WouldBlock)` on saturation. The live pipeline loop treated any write failure as an unrecoverable I/O error and aborted.
28: - **Fix Applied**:
29:   - Dynamically sized `queue_depth` based on `output.buffer_ms` and sample rate in `run.rs`.
30:   - Replaced the fatal `WouldBlock` error with backpressure wait and overrun accounting.
31: 
32: ### B. Extreme Audio Distortion / Clipping
33: - **Symptom**: Sound output was completely mangled, distorted, and unresponsive to volume sliders.
34: - **Cause**: Format mismatch. `PipeWirePcmOutput` hardcodes `AudioFormat::F32LE` (32-bit float) in its format POD, but `audigma-settings` defaulted `[target] sample_format` to `S32Le` (32-bit signed integer). The DSP engine was serializing signed integer PCM bytes, which PipeWire read as floating-point numbers ($\pm 10^{38}$), causing instant rail clipping.
35: - **Fix Applied**: Set `[target] sample_format = "f32"` in configuration.
36: 
37: ### C. Rapid Choppiness & DSP Lifecycle Reset Thrashing
38: - **Symptom**: Audio played at inconsistent speed with constant stuttering/chopping.
39: - **Cause**:
40:   1. `live_pipeline.rs` had an empty-input grace window of only 30 polls $\times 500\mu\text{s} = 15\text{ ms}$. Normal PipeWire quantum delivery (e.g. 1024 frames at 44.1 kHz $\approx 23.2\text{ ms}$) exceeded this threshold.
41:   2. The pipeline falsely declared the stream "idle", reset FIR filter histories, ran a cosine fade-in ramp, and emitted synthetic silence frames into the output.
42: - **Fix Applied**: Expanded the active-streaming grace window in `live_pipeline.rs` to 200 polls ($\approx 100\text{ ms}$).
43: 
44: ### D. Rate Switch Desynchronization
45: - **Symptom**: Switching between tracks with different sample rates caused silent failures or broken output streams.
46: - **Cause**: In `run.rs`, `need_reopen_output` only dropped `current_output = None` when `out_cfg.backend == OutputBackend::Alsa`. When running on PipeWire, the output stream was never recreated on a sample-rate switch.
47: - **Fix Applied**: Dropped `current_output = None` on rate switch regardless of backend.
48: 
49: ### E. DSD Runaway Speed & Audio Distortion (Missing Downsampling & Broken Backpressure)
50: - **Symptom**: DSD input via MPD caused audio output to be mangled/distorted, and Cantata's timeline jumped ahead from ~00:04s to ~00:21s.
51: - **Root Causes**:
52:   1. **`PipelineTopology::resolve` lacked downsampling support**:
53:      When input was DSD64, `PipeWireVirtualSink` decimated DSD to 176.4 kHz PCM. With `pcm_rate_hz = 48000` and `rate_family = "source"`, the output rate resolved to 44.1 kHz. `PipelineTopology::resolve` previously only computed `stages = (target / input).log2()`; for $44100 / 176400 = 0$, it set `stages = 0` and `intermediate_rate = 176400`, passing 176.4 kHz directly into the 44.1 kHz stream (4× sample rate mismatch, causing mangled sound and immediate queue saturation).
54:   2. **`PipeWirePcmOutput::write` silently dropped tiles on overrun**:
55:      After 20 ms of saturation, `write()` incremented `overruns` and returned `Ok(buf.len())`. Discarding tiles destroyed backpressure: the pipeline loop free-ran at CPU speed, draining the virtual sink faster than real time, causing MPD's timeline to skip forward.
56:   3. **Non-RT-safe mutex in PipeWire audio thread**:
57:      `PipeWirePcmOutput` took a `Mutex` lock inside PipeWire's audio callback to unpark the writer thread.
58: - **Fix Applied**:
59:   - **`PipelineTopology`**: Added `decimation_stages` ($2^K$ decimation divider) for same-family downsampling ($176.4\text{k} \to 44.1\text{k}$, $192\text{k} \to 48\text{k}$, $96\text{k} \to 48\text{k}$, $352.8\text{k} \to 44.1\text{k}$).
60:   - **`ChannelDecimatorPool` (`crates/audigma-engine/src/decimator.rs`)**: Implemented a multi-channel power-of-two half-band FIR decimation cascade with partial-chunk residue tracking and zero-copy aligned fast-path. Integrated into `LivePipeline`, `OfflinePipeline`, and `measure_true_peak_pass1`.
61:   - **RT-Safe Backpressure (`PipeWirePcmOutput`)**: Replaced `Mutex<Option<Thread>>` with a lock-free `AtomicPtr<Thread>`. Replaced silent tile dropping with genuine blocking backpressure (bounded by a 2-second timeout), clocking the daemon strictly to PipeWire's playback rate.

89: - **Code finding**: `PipeWirePcmOutput` filled the entire mapped SPA buffer on every callback. Its allocation capacity is not necessarily the number of frames required for the current graph cycle. Overfilling can drain the DSP queue too quickly and undermine playback-paced backpressure.

+# PipeWire output stabilization: current implementation and alternative
+
+## Status and checkpoints
+
+| Implementation | Git checkpoint | Status |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Graph-aware DSD capture (`dsd_clock.rs`) plus preceding output/engine fixes | `master`, commit `c14a518` — `enabled pipewire output (WIP), shortened playback buffer (and latency)` | Retained implementation. User reverified playback after restoration. Quantum-change interruptions remain unresolved. |
+| Pull-driven DSD capture (`dsd_pull.rs`) | `experiment/pipewire-dsd-pull`, commit `2411829` | Archived experiment, **not a replacement for master**. PCM192 silence/unexpected renegotiation and an intermittent segmentation fault were reported. |
+
+The master commit includes both the earlier stabilization work and arbitrary-quantum handling. The formerly staged, pre-arbitrary-quantum baseline is not a separate checkpoint here. The experimental commit is a child of `c14a518`; its two replacement source files were verified byte-for-byte against the saved pull-version backup.
+
+This document consolidates the investigation rather than retaining intermediate builds, obsolete “pending restart” statuses, or step-by-step edit history. No upstream reference checkout was modified.
+
+## 1. Master: consolidated fixes
+
+### Output format, queueing, and lifecycle
+
+- **PCM format agreement:** PipeWire output advertises F32LE; the live test configuration uses `[target] sample_format = "f32"`. Feeding serialized S32LE into that stream had caused severe distortion. This was a configuration correction, not automatic format conversion in the output backend.
+- **Output backpressure:** size the output queue from output buffer duration/rate; wait for space instead of treating ordinary saturation as fatal or silently discarding tiles. The wait retains a bounded timeout rather than allowing unbounded blocking. Previously, discarding tiles let the pipeline run ahead of playback.
+- **Playback demand:** the output callback honors `pw_buffer.requested`, bounded by whole-frame allocation capacity. Only a zero request falls back to aligned capacity. Unconsumed queued bytes are retained; underrun zero-fill is limited to the requested region. The Rust PipeWire `v0_3_50` feature exposes the accessor.
+- **Thread notification/teardown:** replace the output callback's writer-notification mutex with an atomic thread pointer; use acquire publication semantics and join the worker before freeing the notification handle.
+- **Input gaps:** allow approximately 100 ms of empty polling during active playback before emitting idle silence, rather than mistaking normal ~23 ms PipeWire packet spacing for a stopped stream and repeatedly resetting DSP histories/fades.
+- **Rate switches:** reopen the output when its resolved target format/rate changes, including PipeWire output—not only ALSA.
+- **Latency request:** request `quantum_frames_for_rate(rate)/rate` (roughly 21–23 ms) rather than a hardcoded `256/rate`. This aligned normal playback with native DSD buffer duration, but was insufficient by itself when another client or a forced setting changed graph timing.
+
+### Correct downsampling
+
+DSD64 capture decimates to 176.4 kHz PCM. With the test configuration's source-family output selection, the resolved PCM output can be 44.1 kHz. Previously, topology resolution did not implement that downsampling, so 176.4 kHz samples could be delivered to a 44.1 kHz output.
+
+- Add power-of-two same-family decimation to `PipelineTopology`.
+- Add `ChannelDecimatorPool`, a multichannel half-band FIR cascade with partial-chunk residue handling.
+- Integrate it into live/offline pipelines and true-peak analysis, with topology and offline-conversion regression tests.
+
+### Native DSD capture under changing graph quantum/rate
+
+The upstream MPD callback fills `d.maxsize`; it does not limit production to `pw_buffer.requested`. Native DSD passthrough also lacks the PCM adapter's normal rate-match conversion. Consequently, a fixed ~23.2 ms DSD buffer arriving every shorter graph cycle caused runaway input, drops, and seconds of buffered audio—even with correctly paced DSP output.
+
+Examples observed before graph-aware capture:
+- At 256/44100-second graph cycles, an 8192-byte/channel DSD64 packet represents four cycles.
+- Forcing quantum 256 also caused graph-rate renegotiation to 352800 Hz in a later capture; the same packet then represented 32 cycles. The full 128-slot ring held about 2.97 seconds of DSD.
+
+The retained implementation:
+
+1. `GraphCycle` converts actual graph duration/rate to native DSD allocation bytes, rounded to complete interleave groups.
+2. `DsdCaptureClock` accounts graph elapsed time against consumed DSD duration. Credit handles fractional byte counts and oversized old packets; positive credit is capped at one cycle to avoid idle catch-up bursts.
+3. The DSD callback reads `SPA_IO_Position`, publishes requested sizing atomically, and leaves upstream buffers queued when pacing disallows dequeue or the input ring is full. This added scheduling logic does not sleep, lock, or renegotiate from the RT callback.
+4. The control loop requests exact buffer bounds and invalidates `EnumFormat` to trigger active-link reallocation. Updating `Buffers` alone did not initiate re-preparation in the inspected PipeWire implementation.
+5. DSD preroll may start at half the ring slots if small packets cannot provide the configured duration cushion. PCM preroll is unchanged.
+
+Key files: `crates/audigma-io/src/pipewire.rs`, `crates/audigma-io/src/pipewire/dsd_clock.rs`, `crates/audigma-cli/src/commands/run.rs`, and the engine's `topology.rs`, `decimator.rs`, `live_pipeline.rs`, `offline_pipeline.rs`, and `peak.rs`.
+
+### Validation and remaining limitations
+
+- **Before arbitrary-quantum changes:** all nine combinations of PCM44.1/PCM192/DSD64 input against `convertTesting/k17.toml` (ALSA DSD256), `k17.pcm.toml` (ALSA high-rate PCM), and `pipewire.toml` passed listening tests. Repeated PipeWire format switches of at least 20 seconds each also passed.
+- **Final `dsd_clock` implementation:** user verified the three PipeWire input formats and switching, at least 20 seconds each. Quantum sequence 256 → 128 → 64 → 1024 → 4096 had zero input-ring drops and no sustained runaway. Full-ring gating eliminated the transition overflow seen in an earlier build.
+- Longer small-quantum tests still increased PipeWire graph ERR counters, particularly at 64/352800 (~181 µs/cycle). Audigma's `xrun_count == 0` does **not** cover all graph errors or prove uninterrupted playback.
+- User heard silence and an apparent skip around quantum changes, while steady playback speed remained correct. Monitor correlation found a ~24.49 ms forward discontinuity. Active-link reallocation is a plausible contributor, **not an isolated or confirmed sole cause**.
+- After restoring this version, all 41 IO tests, scoped Clippy, formatting, and release build passed; the user subsequently reverified playback and committed it on master. The full nine-case hardware matrix was not repeated specifically after arbitrary-quantum implementation/restoration. MPD stop-delay behavior was not explicitly reconfirmed.
+
+**Architectural assessment:** this is a workaround with a valid graph-time accounting model. Its weak point is coupling packet allocation to scheduling: graph timing changes require asynchronous control-loop renegotiation, while pacing must bridge old-sized packets. Smaller packets also reduce the duration held by a fixed-slot ring. Correct speed and zero input drops do not establish glitch-free transitions.
+
+## 2. Experimental branch: pull-driven DSD capture
+
+### What `2411829` changes
+
+Replaces `dsd_clock.rs` with `dsd_pull.rs` and changes its integration in `pipewire.rs`:
+
+- Native DSD sets `node.driver=true` and pulls its source independently of the hardware playback graph. PCM returns to ordinary follower scheduling.
+- Keep rate-scaled buffer allocation fixed instead of invalidating active-link `EnumFormat` on quantum changes.
+- Request capture only below the configured input cushion, with full-ring protection and one outstanding pull tracked by a native trigger-done listener.
+- Pace pulls using the latest received packet duration, with 5% refill headroom and no accumulated burst credit after a downstream stall. Unpaced 1 ms refill bursts had failed continuity checks with asynchronous `pw-dsdplay`.
+- Count buffered DSD units before publishing the ring chunk, avoiding consumption-before-accounting; retain the small-buffer preroll fallback.
+- Add an ignored silent integration test, `silent_capture_preserves_bytes_across_downstream_stall`, using `AUDIGMA_DSD_TEST_FILE` (stereo DSD64 DSF) and `AUDIGMA_DSD_TEST_EXPECTED` (normalized, byte-interleaved MSB DSD from its beginning).
+
+The intent was to separate allocation from scheduling and avoid discarding in-flight audio during native-link reallocation. That is attractive for DSD, but introduces clock ownership, asynchronous-source coordination, and driven-DSD/follower-PCM transitions. **Architecturally promising is not demonstrated architectural superiority.** Replacing the graph-aware version before equivalent switching coverage was premature.
+
+### What passed—and what did not
+
+- A standalone silent C probe captured ~8.94 seconds byte-for-byte against the DSF. A second run paused pulling for about one second and resumed without byte mismatches.
+- The paced Rust integration passed ten consecutive silent checks: bounded preroll/stalled-consumer buffering, stopped pulling while sufficiently buffered, byte-exact first second after resumption, and zero input drops. These were **DSD-only** checks, not format-switch/output-reopening validation.
+- Formatting, IO tests (39 passed; the environment-dependent silent test ignored by default), scoped Clippy, and release build passed.
+- In an audible quantum-256 test, input buffering stayed ~93–110 ms, with no new input drops, empty polls, or measured hardware graph errors. However, the user heard a brief pause (<0.5 s).
+- The monitor still showed a ~23.22 ms forward jump (1024 frames at 44100 Hz). Neither recording contained a sustained zero run >=1 ms apart from startup padding. The capture may not expose all audible/hardware interruptions; playback versus monitor reconfiguration has not been isolated.
+- **Format-switch regression:** user reported PCM44.1 and DSD64 working, but PCM192 silent. Subsequent switching produced a segmentation fault (exit 139).
+- On a second run, switching did not crash, but logs repeatedly show PCM192 negotiating at 192000 Hz, then unexpectedly renegotiating to 44100 Hz roughly 150 ms later, reopening the output twice. This occurred without another reported track change.
+- Changing clock ownership is a leading suspect for renegotiation, not a confirmed cause. The segmentation fault remains unexplained; no core backtrace was inspected. The second non-crashing run does not clear it.
+- The 1 ms control-loop polling interval has not been validated with sub-millisecond source packets under forced tiny quanta. Independent DSD nodes showed zero timing columns in `pw-top`; those columns are not useful evidence of error-free scheduling.
+
+**Decision:** retain `dsd_clock` on master. The pull branch preserves the failed experiment for investigation; it does not fix the remaining interruption and must not be treated as playback-safe or regression-tested across formats.
+
+## 3. Evidence and resuming the investigation
+
+Diagnostic artifacts are under `/tmp/opencode/`; they are local temporary files, **not durable Git history**:
+
+| Evidence | Files/prefix |
+| --- | --- |
+| Original runaway under forced quantum | `audigma-quantum-test.json` |
+| Final graph-aware quantum sequence and longer steady tests | `audigma-dsd-clock-backpressure-test.json`, `audigma-dsd-clock-steady64-test.json`, `audigma-dsd-clock-steady-moderate-test.json` |

+| Standalone pull probe and byte comparisons | `audigma-dsd-pull-probe.c`, `audigma-dsd-pull-continuity.{log,json}`, `audigma-dsd-pull-backpressure.{log,json}` |

+| Pre-restoration pull source and diffs | `audigma-before-dsd-clock-restore/` (now also preserved by `2411829`) |
+
+The experimental worktree was created at `/tmp/opencode/audigma-dsd-pull-worktree`; use its branch/commit as the durable checkpoint. The user's crash and renegotiation logs were supplied in the conversation, not saved as a separate artifact by this investigation.
+
+For a revisit:
+- Start from the verified master implementation; preserve it while investigating alternatives.
+- Isolate playback discontinuity from monitor-capture reconfiguration before attributing the jump solely to DSD-link reallocation. Removing that reallocation did not remove the measured jump.
+- Investigate the pull branch's core dump and unexpected PCM renegotiation before proposing further architectural changes. Add silent format-switch/output-lifecycle coverage; DSD-only byte continuity is insufficient.

+- Announce immediately before audible tests so the user can listen attentively.

-# PipeWire Output Stabilization (`output.backend = "pipewire"`)
-
-## 1. Context & Motivation
-
-Audigma primarily targets high-performance audiophile hardware output via exclusive ALSA (`output.backend = "alsa"`), which uses a **push model** with hardware-paced blocking DMA backpressure. 
-
-In this session, we tested and diagnosed the live daemon running in full PipeWire loopback mode:
-- `[input] backend = "pipewire"` (virtual sink receiving desktop or MPD streams, including DSD)
-- `[output] backend = "pipewire"` (playback stream routing DSP-upsampled/modulated audio back into the PipeWire desktop graph, e.g. targeting monitor or desktop speakers).
-
-### Test Configuration (`convertTesting/pipewire.toml`)
-We used `convertTesting/pipewire.toml` for live testing against a connected Samsung DisplayPort monitor (native hardware clock 48 kHz).
-
-### Rapid Iteration Workflow
-When testing live audio behavior, we use a quick iteration loop:
-1. (agent) Make targeted edits to code or config.
-2. (agent) Build release: `cargo fmt && cargo build --release`.
-3. (user) Notify the user to test: `./target/release/audigma run -c convertTesting/pipewire.toml`.
-4. (user) Test playback with MPD / Cantata (switching between 44.1k PCM, 192k PCM, and DSD) and reports listening and timing behavior back.
-
----
-
-## 2. Issues Discovered & Root Causes
-
-### A. Immediate Daemon Crash (`I/O error: PipeWire output queue full`)
-- **Symptom**: `audigma run` crashed within milliseconds to seconds with `I/O error: PipeWire output queue full`.
-- **Cause**: `PipeWirePcmOutput` had a hardcoded queue depth of 32 tiles ($\approx 10\text{ ms}$ at 192 kHz). Its `std::io::Write` implementation returned `Err(WouldBlock)` on saturation. The live pipeline loop treated any write failure as an unrecoverable I/O error and aborted.
-- **Fix Applied**:
-  - Dynamically sized `queue_depth` based on `output.buffer_ms` and sample rate in `run.rs`.
-  - Replaced the fatal `WouldBlock` error with backpressure wait and overrun accounting.
-
-### B. Extreme Audio Distortion / Clipping
-- **Symptom**: Sound output was completely mangled, distorted, and unresponsive to volume sliders.
-- **Cause**: Format mismatch. `PipeWirePcmOutput` hardcodes `AudioFormat::F32LE` (32-bit float) in its format POD, but `audigma-settings` defaulted `[target] sample_format` to `S32Le` (32-bit signed integer). The DSP engine was serializing signed integer PCM bytes, which PipeWire read as floating-point numbers ($\pm 10^{38}$), causing instant rail clipping.
-- **Fix Applied**: Set `[target] sample_format = "f32"` in configuration.
-
-### C. Rapid Choppiness & DSP Lifecycle Reset Thrashing
-- **Symptom**: Audio played at inconsistent speed with constant stuttering/chopping.
-- **Cause**:
-  1. `live_pipeline.rs` had an empty-input grace window of only 30 polls $\times 500\mu\text{s} = 15\text{ ms}$. Normal PipeWire quantum delivery (e.g. 1024 frames at 44.1 kHz $\approx 23.2\text{ ms}$) exceeded this threshold.
-  2. The pipeline falsely declared the stream "idle", reset FIR filter histories, ran a cosine fade-in ramp, and emitted synthetic silence frames into the output.
-- **Fix Applied**: Expanded the active-streaming grace window in `live_pipeline.rs` to 200 polls ($\approx 100\text{ ms}$).
-
-### D. Rate Switch Desynchronization
-- **Symptom**: Switching between tracks with different sample rates caused silent failures or broken output streams.
-- **Cause**: In `run.rs`, `need_reopen_output` only dropped `current_output = None` when `out_cfg.backend == OutputBackend::Alsa`. When running on PipeWire, the output stream was never recreated on a sample-rate switch.
-- **Fix Applied**: Dropped `current_output = None` on rate switch regardless of backend.
-
-### E. DSD Runaway Speed & Audio Distortion (Missing Downsampling & Broken Backpressure)
-- **Symptom**: DSD input via MPD caused audio output to be mangled/distorted, and Cantata's timeline jumped ahead from ~00:04s to ~00:21s.
-- **Root Causes**:
-  1. **`PipelineTopology::resolve` lacked downsampling support**:
-     When input was DSD64, `PipeWireVirtualSink` decimated DSD to 176.4 kHz PCM. With `pcm_rate_hz = 48000` and `rate_family = "source"`, the output rate resolved to 44.1 kHz. `PipelineTopology::resolve` previously only computed `stages = (target / input).log2()`; for $44100 / 176400 = 0$, it set `stages = 0` and `intermediate_rate = 176400`, passing 176.4 kHz directly into the 44.1 kHz stream (4× sample rate mismatch, causing mangled sound and immediate queue saturation).
-  2. **`PipeWirePcmOutput::write` silently dropped tiles on overrun**:
-     After 20 ms of saturation, `write()` incremented `overruns` and returned `Ok(buf.len())`. Discarding tiles destroyed backpressure: the pipeline loop free-ran at CPU speed, draining the virtual sink faster than real time, causing MPD's timeline to skip forward.
-  3. **Non-RT-safe mutex in PipeWire audio thread**:
-     `PipeWirePcmOutput` took a `Mutex` lock inside PipeWire's audio callback to unpark the writer thread.
-- **Fix Applied**:
-  - **`PipelineTopology`**: Added `decimation_stages` ($2^K$ decimation divider) for same-family downsampling ($176.4\text{k} \to 44.1\text{k}$, $192\text{k} \to 48\text{k}$, $96\text{k} \to 48\text{k}$, $352.8\text{k} \to 44.1\text{k}$).
-  - **`ChannelDecimatorPool` (`crates/audigma-engine/src/decimator.rs`)**: Implemented a multi-channel power-of-two half-band FIR decimation cascade with partial-chunk residue tracking and zero-copy aligned fast-path. Integrated into `LivePipeline`, `OfflinePipeline`, and `measure_true_peak_pass1`.
-  - **RT-Safe Backpressure (`PipeWirePcmOutput`)**: Replaced `Mutex<Option<Thread>>` with a lock-free `AtomicPtr<Thread>`. Replaced silent tile dropping with genuine blocking backpressure (bounded by a 2-second timeout), clocking the daemon strictly to PipeWire's playback rate.
-
----
-
-## 3. Working State of Changed Files
-
-1. **`crates/audigma-engine/src/topology.rs`**:
-   - Added `decimation_stages` and `decimation_divider()` to `PipelineTopology`.
-   - Added unit tests for same-family downsampling ($176.4\text{k} \to 44.1\text{k}$, $192\text{k} \to 48\text{k}$, $96\text{k} \to 48\text{k}$, etc.).
-2. **`crates/audigma-engine/src/decimator.rs`**:
-   - New `ChannelDecimatorPool` module using `audigma-dsp::fir::HalfBandDecimationCascade`.
-3. **`crates/audigma-engine/src/live_pipeline.rs`**:
-   - Integrated `ChannelDecimatorPool` on input before lifecycle/gain/ASRC.
-   - Sized `in_channels` buffer to `TILE_BASEBAND_FRAMES * dec_divider`.
-   - Extended empty poll grace window to 200 polls (~100 ms).
-4. **`crates/audigma-engine/src/offline_pipeline.rs` & `peak.rs`**:

-   - Added offline downsampling integration tests.

-   - Blocking backpressure without tile discarding.
-6. **`crates/audigma-cli/src/commands/run.rs`**:
-   - Dynamic `queue_depth` based on `buffer_ms` and target sample rate.
-   - Output stream reopening on sample rate change for all backends.
-
----
-
-### F. Output Callback Consumed Allocation Capacity Instead of Requested Frames
-- **Code finding**: `PipeWirePcmOutput` filled the entire mapped SPA buffer on every callback. Its allocation capacity is not necessarily the number of frames required for the current graph cycle. Overfilling can drain the DSP queue too quickly and undermine playback-paced backpressure.
-- **Fix applied (awaiting listening test)**:
-  - Use `pw_buffer.requested` (frames), bounded by whole-frame buffer capacity. Fall back to aligned capacity only when PipeWire supplies no request (`requested == 0`).
-  - Preserve queued bytes beyond the request for subsequent callbacks; zero-fill only within the requested region on underrun.
-  - Enable the Rust PipeWire `v0_3_50` API feature for the requested-frame accessor.
-  - Fix notification-handle publication with an acquire load, and join the output worker before freeing the handle so an in-flight callback cannot dereference freed memory during rate-switch teardown.
-- **Validation**: Three output sizing regression tests, decimator tests, topology tests, and offline pipeline integration tests pass. Release build succeeds.
-- **Status**: This corrects an output pacing defect, but its connection to the remaining DSD64 timeline skips still needs live confirmation. ALSA paths and the test configuration are unchanged.
-

+
+## Status and checkpoints
+
+| Implementation | Git checkpoint | Status |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Graph-aware DSD capture (`dsd_clock.rs`) plus preceding output/engine fixes | `master`, commit `c14a518` — `enabled pipewire output (WIP), shortened playback buffer (and latency)` | Retained implementation. +
+The master commit includes both the earlier stabilization work and arbitrary-quantum handling. The formerly staged, pre-arbitrary-quantum baseline is not a separate checkpoint here. The experimental commit is a child of `c14a518`; its two replacement source files were verified byte-for-byte against the saved pull-version backup.
+
+This document consolidates the investigation rather than retaining intermediate builds, obsolete “pending restart” statuses, or step-by-step edit history. No upstream reference checkout was modified.

+## 1. Master: consolidated fixes
+
+### Output format, queueing, and lifecycle
+
+- **PCM format agreement:** PipeWire output advertises F32LE; the live test configuration uses `[target] sample_format = "f32"`. Feeding serialized S32LE into that stream had caused severe distortion. This was a configuration correction, not automatic format conversion in the output backend.
+- **Output backpressure:** size the output queue from output buffer duration/rate; wait for space instead of treating ordinary saturation as fatal or silently discarding tiles. The wait retains a bounded timeout rather than allowing unbounded blocking. Previously, discarding tiles let the pipeline run ahead of playback.
+- **Playback demand:** the output callback honors `pw_buffer.requested`, bounded by whole-frame allocation capacity. Only a zero request falls back to aligned capacity. Unconsumed queued bytes are retained; underrun zero-fill is limited to the requested region. The Rust PipeWire `v0_3_50` feature exposes the accessor.
+- **Thread notification/teardown:** replace the output callback's writer-notification mutex with an atomic thread pointer; use acquire publication semantics and join the worker before freeing the notification handle.
+- **Input gaps:** allow approximately 100 ms of empty polling during active playback before emitting idle silence, rather than mistaking normal ~23 ms PipeWire packet spacing for a stopped stream and repeatedly resetting DSP histories/fades.
+- **Rate switches:** reopen the output when its resolved target format/rate changes, including PipeWire output—not only ALSA.
+- **Latency request:** request `quantum_frames_for_rate(rate)/rate` (roughly 21–23 ms) rather than a hardcoded `256/rate`. This aligned normal playback with native DSD buffer duration, but was insufficient by itself when another client or a forced setting changed graph timing.
+
+### Correct downsampling
+
+DSD64 capture decimates to 176.4 kHz PCM. With the test configuration's source-family output selection, the resolved PCM output can be 44.1 kHz. Previously, topology resolution did not implement that downsampling, so 176.4 kHz samples could be delivered to a 44.1 kHz output.
+
+- Add power-of-two same-family decimation to `PipelineTopology`.
+- Add `ChannelDecimatorPool`, a multichannel half-band FIR cascade with partial-chunk residue handling.
+- Integrate it into live/offline pipelines and true-peak analysis, with topology and offline-conversion regression tests.
+
+### Native DSD capture under changing graph quantum/rate
+
+The upstream MPD callback fills `d.maxsize`; it does not limit production to `pw_buffer.requested`. Native DSD passthrough also lacks the PCM adapter's normal rate-match conversion. Consequently, a fixed ~23.2 ms DSD buffer arriving every shorter graph cycle caused runaway input, drops, and seconds of buffered audio—even with correctly paced DSP output.
+
+Examples observed before graph-aware capture:
+- At 256/44100-second graph cycles, an 8192-byte/channel DSD64 packet represents four cycles.
+- Forcing quantum 256 also caused graph-rate renegotiation to 352800 Hz in a later capture; the same packet then represented 32 cycles. The full 128-slot ring held about 2.97 seconds of DSD.
+
+The retained implementation:
+
+1. `GraphCycle` converts actual graph duration/rate to native DSD allocation bytes, rounded to complete interleave groups.
+2. `DsdCaptureClock` accounts graph elapsed time against consumed DSD duration. Credit handles fractional byte counts and oversized old packets; positive credit is capped at one cycle to avoid idle catch-up bursts.
+3. The DSD callback reads `SPA_IO_Position`, publishes requested sizing atomically, and leaves upstream buffers queued when pacing disallows dequeue or the input ring is full. This added scheduling logic does not sleep, lock, or renegotiate from the RT callback.
+4. The control loop requests exact buffer bounds and invalidates `EnumFormat` to trigger active-link reallocation. Updating `Buffers` alone did not initiate re-preparation in the inspected PipeWire implementation.
+5. DSD preroll may start at half the ring slots if small packets cannot provide the configured duration cushion. PCM preroll is unchanged.
+
+Key files: `crates/audigma-io/src/pipewire.rs`, `crates/audigma-io/src/pipewire/dsd_clock.rs`, `crates/audigma-cli/src/commands/run.rs`, and the engine's `topology.rs`, `decimator.rs`, `live_pipeline.rs`, `offline_pipeline.rs`, and `peak.rs`.
+
+### Validation and remaining limitations
+
+- **Before arbitrary-quantum changes:** all nine combinations of PCM44.1/PCM192/DSD64 input against `convertTesting/k17.toml` (ALSA DSD256), `k17.pcm.toml` (ALSA high-rate PCM), and `pipewire.toml` passed listening tests. Repeated PipeWire format switches of at least 20 seconds each also passed.
+- **Final `dsd_clock` implementation:** user verified the three PipeWire input formats and switching, at least 20 seconds each. Quantum sequence 256 → 128 → 64 → 1024 → 4096 had zero input-ring drops and no sustained runaway. Full-ring gating eliminated the transition overflow seen in an earlier build.
+- Longer small-quantum tests still increased PipeWire graph ERR counters, particularly at 64/352800 (~181 µs/cycle). Audigma's `xrun_count == 0` does **not** cover all graph errors or prove uninterrupted playback.
+- User heard silence and an apparent skip around quantum changes, while steady playback speed remained correct. Monitor correlation found a ~24.49 ms forward discontinuity. Active-link reallocation is a plausible contributor, **not an isolated or confirmed sole cause**.
+- After restoring this version, all 41 IO tests, scoped Clippy, formatting, and release build passed; the user subsequently reverified playback and committed it on master. The full nine-case hardware matrix was not repeated specifically after arbitrary-quantum implementation/restoration. MPD stop-delay behavior was not explicitly reconfirmed.
+
+**Architectural assessment:** this is a workaround with a valid graph-time accounting model. Its weak point is coupling packet allocation to scheduling: graph timing changes require asynchronous control-loop renegotiation, while pacing must bridge old-sized packets. Smaller packets also reduce the duration held by a fixed-slot ring. Correct speed and zero input drops do not establish glitch-free transitions.

+## 2. Experimental branch: pull-driven DSD capture
+
+### What `2411829` changes
+
+Replaces `dsd_clock.rs` with `dsd_pull.rs` and changes its integration in `pipewire.rs`:
+
+- Native DSD sets `node.driver=true` and pulls its source independently of the hardware playback graph. PCM returns to ordinary follower scheduling.
+- Keep rate-scaled buffer allocation fixed instead of invalidating active-link `EnumFormat` on quantum changes.
+- Request capture only below the configured input cushion, with full-ring protection and one outstanding pull tracked by a native trigger-done listener.
+- Pace pulls using the latest received packet duration, with 5% refill headroom and no accumulated burst credit after a downstream stall. Unpaced 1 ms refill bursts had failed continuity checks with asynchronous `pw-dsdplay`.
+- Count buffered DSD units before publishing the ring chunk, avoiding consumption-before-accounting; retain the small-buffer preroll fallback.
+- Add an ignored silent integration test, `silent_capture_preserves_bytes_across_downstream_stall`, using `AUDIGMA_DSD_TEST_FILE` (stereo DSD64 DSF) and `AUDIGMA_DSD_TEST_EXPECTED` (normalized, byte-interleaved MSB DSD from its beginning).
+
+The intent was to separate allocation from scheduling and avoid discarding in-flight audio during native-link reallocation. That is attractive for DSD, but introduces clock ownership, asynchronous-source coordination, and driven-DSD/follower-PCM transitions. **Architecturally promising is not demonstrated architectural superiority.** Replacing the graph-aware version before equivalent switching coverage was premature.
+
+### What passed—and what did not
+
+- A standalone silent C probe captured ~8.94 seconds byte-for-byte against the DSF. A second run paused pulling for about one second and resumed without byte mismatches.
+- The paced Rust integration passed ten consecutive silent checks: bounded preroll/stalled-consumer buffering, stopped pulling while sufficiently buffered, byte-exact first second after resumption, and zero input drops. These were **DSD-only** checks, not format-switch/output-reopening validation.
+- Formatting, IO tests (39 passed; the environment-dependent silent test ignored by default), scoped Clippy, and release build passed.
+- In an audible quantum-256 test, input buffering stayed ~93–110 ms, with no new input drops, empty polls, or measured hardware graph errors. However, the user heard a brief pause (<0.5 s).
+- The monitor still showed a ~23.22 ms forward jump (1024 frames at 44100 Hz). Neither recording contained a sustained zero run >=1 ms apart from startup padding. The capture may not expose all audible/hardware interruptions; playback versus monitor reconfiguration has not been isolated.
+- **Format-switch regression:** user reported PCM44.1 and DSD64 working, but PCM192 silent. Subsequent switching produced a segmentation fault (exit 139).
+- On a second run, switching did not crash, but logs repeatedly show PCM192 negotiating at 192000 Hz, then unexpectedly renegotiating to 44100 Hz roughly 150 ms later, reopening the output twice. This occurred without another reported track change.
+- Changing clock ownership is a leading suspect for renegotiation, not a confirmed cause. The segmentation fault remains unexplained; no core backtrace was inspected. The second non-crashing run does not clear it.
+- The 1 ms control-loop polling interval has not been validated with sub-millisecond source packets under forced tiny quanta. Independent DSD nodes showed zero timing columns in `pw-top`; those columns are not useful evidence of error-free scheduling.
+
+**Decision:** retain `dsd_clock` on master. The pull branch preserves the failed experiment for investigation; it does not fix the remaining interruption and must not be treated as playback-safe or regression-tested across formats.

26: ### Correct downsampling
27: 
28: DSD64 capture decimates to 176.4 kHz PCM. With the test configuration's source-family output selection, the resolved PCM output can be 44.1 kHz. Previously, topology resolution did not implement that downsampling, so 176.4 kHz samples could be delivered to a 44.1 kHz output.

30: - Add power-of-two same-family decimation to `PipelineTopology`.
31: - Add `ChannelDecimatorPool`, a multichannel half-band FIR cascade with partial-chunk residue handling.

34: ### Native DSD capture under changing graph quantum/rate
35: 
36: The upstream MPD callback fills `d.maxsize`; it does not limit production to `pw_buffer.requested`. Native DSD passthrough also lacks the PCM adapter's normal rate-match conversion. Consequently, a fixed ~23.2 ms DSD buffer arriving every shorter graph cycle caused runaway input, drops, and seconds of buffered audio—even with correctly paced DSP output.

38: Examples observed before graph-aware capture:
39: - At 256/44100-second graph cycles, an 8192-byte/channel DSD64 packet represents four cycles.

41: 
42: The retained implementation:
43: 
44: 1. `GraphCycle` converts actual graph duration/rate to native DSD allocation bytes, rounded to complete interleave groups.
45: 2. `DsdCaptureClock` accounts graph elapsed time against consumed DSD duration. Credit handles fractional byte counts and oversized old packets; positive credit is capped at one cycle to avoid idle catch-up bursts.
46: 3. The DSD callback reads `SPA_IO_Position`, publishes requested sizing atomically, and leaves upstream buffers queued when pacing disallows dequeue or the input ring is full. This added scheduling logic does not sleep, lock, or renegotiate from the RT callback.
47: 4. The control loop requests exact buffer bounds and invalidates `EnumFormat` to trigger active-link reallocation. Updating `Buffers` alone did not initiate re-preparation in the inspected PipeWire implementation.
48: 5. DSD preroll may start at half the ring slots if small packets cannot provide the configured duration cushion. PCM preroll is unchanged.

53: 
54: - **Before arbitrary-quantum changes:** all nine combinations of PCM44.1/PCM192/DSD64 input against `convertTesting/k17.toml` (ALSA DSD256), `k17.pcm.toml` (ALSA high-rate PCM), and `pipewire.toml` passed listening tests. 57: - User heard silence and an apparent skip around quantum changes, while steady playback speed remained correct. Monitor correlation found a ~24.49 ms forward discontinuity. Active-link reallocation is a plausible contributor, **not an isolated or confirmed sole cause**.
58: - After restoring this version, all 41 IO tests, scoped Clippy, formatting, and release build passed; the user subsequently reverified playback and committed it on master. The full nine-case hardware matrix was not repeated specifically after arbitrary-quantum implementation/restoration. MPD stop-delay behavior was not explicitly reconfirmed.
59: 
60: **Architectural assessment:** this is a workaround with a valid graph-time accounting model. Its weak point is coupling packet allocation to scheduling: graph timing changes require asynchronous control-loop renegotiation, while pacing must bridge old-sized packets. Smaller packets also reduce the duration held by a fixed-slot ring. Correct speed and zero input drops do not establish glitch-free transitions.

66: Replaces `dsd_clock.rs` with `dsd_pull.rs` and changes its integration in `pipewire.rs`:

68: - Native DSD sets `node.driver=true` and pulls its source independently of the hardware playback graph. PCM returns to ordinary follower scheduling.
